overview: Algeria is the largest country in Africa, on the Mediterranean coast of North Africa. Its capital and largest city is Algiers. Algeria was ruled by France from 1830 and won its independence in 1962 after a long war. Arabic and Berber (Tamazight) are official languages, and the country is a major producer of oil and natural gas.

geography.text: More than four-fifths of Algeria lies in the Sahara Desert, with vast seas of sand, rocky plateaus and the Hoggar Mountains in the south. Most people live in the north, along the Mediterranean coast and in the fertile valleys and plains among the Atlas Mountains.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Mediterranean on the coast, and extremely hot and dry in the Sahara.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Fennec foxes, Barbary macaques and dorcas gazelles.

history.text: Berber kingdoms ruled the region in ancient times, followed by Rome. Arab armies brought Islam in the 600s, and later Algiers was part of the Ottoman world. France invaded in 1830 and ruled for 132 years. After a war of independence from 1954 to 1962, in which hundreds of thousands died, Algeria became independent. A civil war in the 1990s cost many more lives.

events.title: Emir Abdelkader
events.text: Abdelkader leads resistance against France for 15 years.

events.title: War of independence
events.text: The FLN begins its armed struggle.

events.title: Civil war
events.text: A cancelled election leads to a decade of conflict.

government.text: Algeria is a semi-presidential republic. The President, elected every five years, holds strong powers and appoints the Prime Minister. The army has long had great influence. In 2019 mass peaceful protests, called the Hirak, forced President Bouteflika to resign after 20 years.

economy.text: Oil and natural gas make up almost all of Algeria's exports, and it is a major gas supplier to Europe through pipelines under the Mediterranean. The state controls much of the economy, and many young people struggle to find jobs.

culture.text: Algeria is the largest country in Africa. Its culture mixes Arab, Amazigh (Berber) and French influences; Arabic and Tamazight are official languages. Raï music, from Oran, became popular worldwide. The Sahara covers more than four-fifths of the country.

items.title: Raï
items.text: Popular music from Oran, listed by UNESCO in 2022.

items.title: Tassili n'Ajjer
items.text: Thousands of ancient rock paintings in the Sahara.

items.title: Casbah of Algiers
items.text: An old citadel city listed by UNESCO.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Couscous, listed by UNESCO, and chakhchoukha, a stew with torn flatbread.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Raï music from Oran and Andalusian classical music.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Yennayer, the Amazigh New Year in January, is a national holiday.

sport.text: Football is Algeria's passion. It won the Africa Cup of Nations in 1990 and 2019 and reached the last 16 of the 2014 World Cup. Runners such as Noureddine Morceli and Taoufik Makhloufi have won world and Olympic titles.
